g_rules.text: Every post follows ICP pain -> author's proof -> Build Room as the bridge
Activate exactly one ICP emotion per post (fear, frustration, aspiration, identity, relief); hook names it, body resolves it
Every post needs one proof anchor, placed in the body after the hook
Never invent proof; only use numbers the author can verify
Anchor type chosen by angle (own result -> personal story [default]; possibility -> member win; mistake/pattern -> coaching moment)
Don't repeat ICP emotion, anchor type or angle used in the last 10 posts
Setup line after hook is a fixed 'Here's ...:' scroll-stop formula
Pivot: one-sentence insight/shift that made it possible
Payoff: what the ICP gets, in their dream-outcome language
CTA defaults to The Build Room, which must be named in the bridge line right before the CTA
CTA line exactly: Comment "KEYWORD" and I'll send you the link. (nothing appended)
Keyword is a fun non-offensive noun (food, animal, object), easy to type, unrelated to topic
Keyword must not already appear in the funnel-log registry
Hook is the first 1-2 lines: one sentence, two max
Hook has a specific number, dollar amount, timeframe or result; never vague
Hook is first person ('I'), never third person, never a quote
Hook has no ellipsis and no exclamation marks; confident not hyped
Hook pattern chosen by content-type mapping (9 named patterns, e.g. Confession / Gap Reveal, Breaking News + Speed Flex)
Hook pattern variety: don't reuse a pattern from the last 2-3 posts
Choose Format A/B/C/D based on post angle, not randomly
Format A template: hook, bridge, credibility line, specific arrow list, pain reframe ('The biggest X isn't Y. It's Z.'), proof anchor, CTA, PS
Format A: embed at least one 'No X. No Y. Just Z.' line inside the arrow list
$5/day cost anchor whenever the post involves AI tooling
Format B story template: confession/bold hook, one-line setup, 3-4 short paragraphs problem->tension->shift->result, 1-2 line lesson; lead with the Before state
Format C curator template: '[Big number] [things] exist. Most are garbage.' + 'Here's what actually works:' + 5-7 arrow items
Format D community-proof template: 'A [person type] in my community [outcome]...', what they built, what made it possible, 'You don't need [prerequisite].'
Never name a community member without consent; default to 'a [person] in my community' + specifics
Hook, CTA and PS are always present regardless of format
Every post ends with a PS (instead of a repost line)
PS is Hormozi-style: make inaction feel expensive, using one of 5 formulas (cost of inaction, identity split, reframe decision, permission removal, mirror challenge)
PS is 1-2 sentences max
PS never pitches the offer directly
PS never uses an em dash
PS matched to the post's specific ICP fear/objection
Rotate PS formula; don't default to identity split
Voice direct and self-assured, matter-of-fact about results, not humble-braggy
First person always
Specific over generic ('195 posts' not 'a lot of posts')
Casual but sharp; contractions fine
Anti-corporate: no 'leverage synergies', 'actionable insights', 'game-changer'
Occasionally raw phrasing is on-brand
Generous framing: CTAs offer value, not demands
Third-grade reading level: short words, break sentences over 10 words, no jargon, no acronyms
Use ICP language verbatim when available
No internal tool names (TrendJacker, Brand Genius, Blotato, LeadShark) in body; use plain descriptions
Use → for positive bullet lists
Use 𐄂 for negative/didn't-do lists
Use 1/, 2/, 3/ for numbered steps (not 1.)
1-3 sentences per paragraph, most are 1
Blank line between every paragraph
No headers, no bold, no markdown in post body
CTA keyword in quotes
Primary proof anchor uses author's stats ('200K+ followers. $150K+ in content revenue. This is the system.'); vary framing not numbers
Objection removers ('No X. No Y. Just Z.') embedded inside the arrow list, never a separate section
Output the full ready-to-paste post with no preamble
After the post: '---' then 'Hook formula used: [pattern name] — for A/B tracking. Strip before publishing.'
Written in Duncan's persona (creator/Build Room owner)
Never ask people to follow; give value and let the post work
Every post must pass the positioning filter (connect topic to brand/audience)
If a hook pattern yields a weak first line, try the next best pattern; adapt templates, don't copy verbatim
